headline: Markets idle before the Fed; Canada hikes, oil tops $102
summary: Stocks are flat to slightly higher and bitcoin is holding near $80,600 as traders wait for the Fed's 2 p.m. decision, which is widely expected to be a hold with a warning that more hikes are possible. The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5% this morning, its first increase since 2023, because the oil shock is keeping inflation near 3%. U.S. crude is up about 2.5% to $102 after Yemen's Houthis claimed a strike on a Saudi refinery, and the 10-year Treasury yield is back above 5%.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin is steady and spot bitcoin ETFs took in money two days running, but ether and most large altcoins are down 5–16% over the past month and the Fear & Greed index sits at a neutral 51.

stocks.label: Mixed
stocks.why: The S&P 500 is within about 1.5% of its record and volatility is low (VIX about 17), but 5% bond yields, $100 oil and doubts about AI spending after Meta's slide are keeping buyers selective.

drivers.title: Fed decision at 2 p.m. ET
drivers.detail: The Fed's target range is 3.75%–4.00% after a September hike, and markets price only about a 5% chance of another increase today. The focus is Chair Kevin Warsh's tone: September CPI ran at 3.7%, and a 'hawkish pause' that points to a December hike would weigh on rate-sensitive assets.
drivers.assets: All markets, especially bitcoin and tech stocks

drivers.title: Bank of Canada hikes to 2.5%
drivers.detail: The Bank raised its policy rate a quarter point, its first hike since July 2023, saying it wants to stop high energy prices from spreading into other prices; headline inflation is about 3% and expected near 3.5% by year-end. It kept the door open to more hikes, which means prime-linked borrowing such as variable mortgages and HELOCs gets more expensive.
drivers.assets: Canadian banks, real estate, variable-rate borrowers; supportive for the loonie

drivers.title: Oil back above $100
drivers.detail: U.S. crude is up about 2.5% to $102 and Brent is near $115 after Yemen's Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, which Riyadh has not confirmed. Pricey oil helps Canadian energy producers but feeds the inflation that is pushing central banks to hike.
drivers.assets: Oil, CNQ and TSX energy, airlines, inflation outlook

drivers.title: 10-year yield back above 5%
drivers.detail: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.03%, near the top of its range for the year. High 'risk-free' returns make it harder for richly valued stocks and non-yielding assets like bitcoin and gold to attract new money.

drivers.title: Big Tech earnings and the AI spending question
drivers.detail: Microsoft and Alphabet report after today's close and Amazon tomorrow, a week after Meta fell about 12% when it signalled heavy spending again in 2027. Meanwhile SK Hynix's record quarter and Broadcom's reported $63 billion AI-compute financing package are lifting chip stocks.

drivers.title: Crypto ETF flows split
drivers.detail: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds that hold the coin for stock-market investors) took in about $176 million on Tuesday, their second straight day of inflows. Ether ETFs have lost more than $1 billion in October, their worst month of 2026.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Up 0.3% in 24h but down 4.0% this week and 3.8% over 30 days, at about $80,600
crypto.why: Bitcoin has spent the week pinned around $80,000 as traders wait for the Fed; its 24-hour range was roughly $79,800 to $81,600. Spot bitcoin ETFs drew about $286 million over Monday and Tuesday, and coins leaving exchanges hit a five-week high, both signs of buyers taking coins off the market. Offsetting that, leverage is being cut: open interest (the value of open futures bets) slipped about 1% to $38.4 billion, and Glassnode reported big Hyperliquid traders turned net short bitcoin for the first time since March.
crypto.meaning: Bitcoin is about 36% below its record of roughly $126,000 and is trading like a rate-sensitive asset, so tonight's Fed tone matters more than crypto-specific news. Holders should expect choppy moves around 2 p.m. and again during Thursday's inflation data and Friday's large monthly options expiry.

outlook.bullCase: A Fed hold without a clear December-hike signal, plus continued ETF inflows, could push it through the $81,800–$84,000 zone that capped the range, opening a move toward the mid-$80,000s.
outlook.bearCase: A hawkish Warsh or hot PCE inflation data could break the $79,800 floor; the next support traders cite is near the 100-day average around $77,700, and Strategy's average buy price near $75,400 is a psychological level.
outlook.watch: Fed statement and press conference (today), PCE inflation (Thursday), daily ETF flows, Friday's Deribit options expiry, and whether $79,800 holds on a daily close.

crypto.name: Ether
crypto.move: Down 0.2% in 24h, 5.8% this week and 13.4% over 30 days, at about $2,336
crypto.why: Ether has lagged bitcoin all month: U.S. spot ether ETFs saw about $1.08 billion of outflows in October through Oct. 21, the biggest monthly outflow of 2026, wiping out September's inflows. The ETH/BTC ratio has slipped to about 0.029, meaning ether keeps losing ground to bitcoin. Ether ETFs lost another $240 million over the last five sessions even as bitcoin funds turned positive.
crypto.meaning: Ether is down roughly 18% for the year and big funds are still trimming, so rallies have been sold quickly. Its moves tend to be larger than bitcoin's in both directions around macro events like today's Fed decision.

outlook.bullCase: A soft Fed outcome and a turn to ETF inflows could lift it back to $2,450–$2,700, where it started October.
outlook.bearCase: If outflows continue and bitcoin loses $79,800, ether could slide toward the low $2,200s or $2,000.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the ETH/BTC ratio (a rise above 0.030 would signal relative strength), and the Fed and PCE outcomes.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Up 0.3% in 24h but down 5.6% this week and 15.9% over 30 days, at about $101
crypto.why: Solana has followed the broad altcoin sell-off this month and is now sitting right on the $100 round number. There's no single Solana-specific shock; the drop tracks the risk-off mood in altcoins, high bond yields and fading speculative volume. Spot Solana ETFs have had a long streak of positive weekly inflows this year, which has helped cushion declines.
crypto.meaning: $100 is a widely watched level, so a clean break either way could trigger outsized moves. For holders, Solana remains a higher-beta bet on the overall crypto mood rather than on its own news right now.

outlook.bullCase: Holding $100 and a calm Fed could bring a rebound toward $110–$120, the area analysts flagged earlier in the ETF inflow streak.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close well below $100 could send it toward the low $90s.
outlook.watch: Daily closes around $100, Solana ETF flows, and bitcoin's reaction to the Fed.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Down 0.6% in 24h, 3.4% this week and 13.7% over 30 days, at about $1.31
crypto.why: XRP has drifted lower with the rest of the large altcoins through October, with no major company-specific catalyst in the past day. Its decline is mostly about the broad pullback in risk appetite and lighter trading.
crypto.meaning: XRP is behaving like the rest of the large-cap altcoin pack, so macro news and bitcoin's direction are likely to dominate its next move.

outlook.bullCase: A broad crypto bounce after the Fed could take it back toward $1.45–$1.50, where it traded earlier in the month.
outlook.bearCase: Further altcoin weakness could push it toward $1.20.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin's reaction to the Fed and overall altcoin volume.

crypto.name: Hyperliquid
crypto.move: Up 0.9% in 24h, down 1.0% this week and 10.4% over 30 days, at about $80
crypto.why: HYPE has held up better than most altcoins this week. On Oct. 27, Kraken's parent Payward said it plans to be the first CFTC-regulated firm to deploy markets on Hyperliquid's HIP-3 system (pending approval), and NEAR used Hyperliquid's infrastructure for pre-IPO perpetual futures. Hyperliquid directs almost all fees from new markets to buying back and burning HYPE, which supports demand.
crypto.meaning: HYPE is tied to trading activity on the exchange, so it does best when traders are active and leverage is rising. Open interest is about 15% below its early-October peak, which caps near-term upside.

outlook.bullCase: Regulatory progress on the Kraken/Bitnomial plan and rising trading volume could push it back toward its record area near $89.
outlook.bearCase: A crypto-wide drop that cuts trading volumes could send it into the low $70s.
outlook.watch: Hyperliquid open interest and fee revenue, CFTC news on the HIP-3 deployment, and bitcoin's direction.

sources.title: CoinMarketCap: Hyperliquid latest updates

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Down 1.0% in 24h, 3.0% this week and 19.5% over 30 days, at about $1,275
crypto.why: Zcash, a privacy-focused coin, is still up about 136% this year but has cooled since its autumn spike toward $1,700. Its NU7 network upgrade is due on Nov. 5 and will cut settlement times from about 75 seconds to 25. Zcash-linked ETFs took in about $21 million in a recent four-day stretch, and use of its private 'shielded' transactions has climbed back to about 50%.
crypto.meaning: Upgrades often bring a 'buy the rumour, sell the news' pattern, so volatility around Nov. 5 is likely. ZEC moves far more than bitcoin and is a high-risk holding.

outlook.bullCase: A smooth NU7 launch and ETF inflows could drive a break above $1,400, with analysts eyeing a retest of the $1,700 area.
outlook.bearCase: Profit-taking after the upgrade or a bitcoin slide could push it toward $1,000, and below that toward about $800.
outlook.watch: The Nov. 5 NU7 activation, ETF flows, and the $1,000 and $1,400 levels.

sources.title: FXEmpire: ZEC holds $1,000 support ahead of NU7

crypto.name: Pepe
crypto.move: Up 10.5% in 24h, 4.7% this week and 13.2% over 30 days, at about $0.00000485
crypto.why: Pepe, a meme coin with no product behind it, is the biggest large-cap gainer today. Crypto analysis sites flagged a jump of as much as 14.5% on Oct. 28; we found no fundamental news, so the move looks driven by speculative buying and traders rotating into meme coins while bitcoin stalls.
crypto.meaning: Meme-coin rallies like this often fade as fast as they start. Anyone holding it is betting on crowd sentiment rather than earnings or usage.

outlook.bullCase: If risk appetite returns after the Fed and meme-coin volume stays high, it could extend toward its early-October highs.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin weakens, meme coins usually fall hardest; giving back today's 10% gain would be typical.
outlook.watch: Trading volume, bitcoin's direction, and whether the gain holds for more than a day or two.

sources.title: Crypto & Finance market report, Oct. 28

crypto.name: Ethena
crypto.move: Down 6.8% in 24h, 6.2% this week and 27.8% over 30 days, at about $0.196
crypto.why: Ethena's governance token is one of today's weakest large coins and is testing its $0.19–$0.20 support zone. Selling pressure has built after BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes reportedly sold 14 million ENA and a dYdX vote on delisting ENA markets ends Oct. 29. The planned wind-down of Balancer, where some pools hold Ethena positions, moves to withdrawals-only on Oct. 30.
crypto.meaning: ENA is down over 90% from its record and has several near-term overhangs. Holders face a high-risk setup where a support break could accelerate selling.

outlook.bullCase: Holding $0.19 and a calm dYdX/Balancer outcome could allow a rebound to $0.21–$0.23.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close below $0.19 opens a move toward $0.18 or lower.
outlook.watch: The dYdX delisting vote (Oct. 29), Balancer withdrawals (Oct. 30), and the $0.19 level.

sources.title: CoinMarketCap: Ethena price analysis

crypto.name: Bitway
crypto.move: Up 16.0% in 24h, 8.6% this week and 28.8% over 30 days, at about $1.75
crypto.why: Bitway, a crypto project whose seed round was led by TRON, is today's biggest top-100 gainer, bouncing after falling about 17% in a week from a peak above $2.60. Its earlier run of thousands of percent in mid-October was fuelled by Binance Wallet campaigns, a Bitrue listing and forced closing of short bets (short liquidations). Ownership is extremely concentrated: data cited by CoinMarketCap shows the top 100 wallets hold about 99.9% of supply and the two largest about 85%.
crypto.meaning: With so few wallets controlling supply, a handful of sellers can move the price sharply. A token unlock (new tokens released to insiders) is listed for around Nov. 2, which could add selling pressure.

outlook.bullCase: Continued exchange promotions and short squeezes could retest $2.00–$2.60.
outlook.bearCase: Selling from large wallets or around the scheduled unlock could drag it back below $1.50.
outlook.watch: The early-November unlock, large-wallet transfers to exchanges, and the $1.86 level (its 50-day average, which it has struggled to hold).

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Up 0.15% today to about 7,734; down 0.3% this week
stocks.why: U.S. stocks are treading water before the Fed decision and tonight's Microsoft and Alphabet results. Chipmakers are leading after SK Hynix posted a record quarter and Broadcom's reported $63 billion AI-compute financing deal, while Robinhood is dragging after weak results. Seasonality is a talking point: the historically strong November–April stretch starts Monday.
stocks.meaning: The index is about 1.4% below its 52-week high, so the bar for upside surprises is high. A 5% 10-year yield is the main headwind for valuations.

outlook.bullCase: A Fed hold without strong hike talk and solid Big Tech earnings could push it to a new high above about 7,845.
outlook.bearCase: A hawkish Fed, a disappointing cloud or AI-spending outlook, or another oil spike could send it back toward 7,600 or lower.
outlook.watch: Fed statement and Warsh's press conference, MSFT/GOOGL tonight and AMZN Thursday, PCE inflation Thursday.

stocks.name: Nasdaq Composite
stocks.move: Down 0.07% today to about 26,460; down 0.9% this week
stocks.why: The tech-heavy Nasdaq is flat as gains in chip stocks like AMD and Broadcom offset losses in Meta, Tesla and Microsoft. Investors are waiting to hear whether Microsoft and Alphabet can show AI spending is paying off, after Meta's selloff last week revived worries about huge capital budgets.
stocks.meaning: Tonight's earnings could move the index 1–2% on Thursday. The Nasdaq is about 4.5% below its 52-week high and remains the most sensitive major index to bond yields.

outlook.bullCase: Strong Azure and Google Cloud growth with steady spending plans could lift it back toward 27,000+.
outlook.bearCase: Higher capex without matching revenue, or a hawkish Fed, could send it toward 25,900, last week's low.
outlook.watch: MSFT and GOOGL after the close, AMZN Thursday, and the 10-year yield.

stocks.name: S&P/TSX Composite
stocks.move: Flat today at about 36,170; down 0.4% this week
stocks.why: Toronto stocks are flat as the Bank of Canada's quarter-point hike weighs on rate-sensitive names while energy producers rise with oil above $102. Banks are slightly lower after the hike, which squeezes borrowers but can widen lending margins.
stocks.meaning: The TSX's heavy weighting in energy and banks makes it a mix of winners and losers from today's news. It is about 2.4% below its 52-week high.

outlook.bullCase: Firm oil prices and good bank earnings later in the season could carry it back toward 37,000.
outlook.bearCase: If the BoC signals more hikes or oil drops sharply, it could slip toward 35,500.
outlook.watch: Oil prices, BoC commentary, Canadian GDP data, and Shopify earnings on Nov. 3.

stocks.name: U.S. crude oil
stocks.move: Up 2.5% today to about $102.40 a barrel; up about 5% this week
stocks.why: Oil is climbing again after Yemen's Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery; Riyadh has not confirmed damage. Prices have stayed high for months because of the conflict involving Iran, with Brent near $115.
stocks.meaning: Oil above $100 is the main reason inflation is sticky in both Canada and the U.S., and why both central banks are leaning toward hikes. It also lifts gas prices for Ontario drivers.

outlook.bullCase: Confirmed damage to Saudi facilities or new attacks on Gulf shipping could push it toward $110–$119, this year's high.
outlook.bearCase: Signs of de-escalation or an emergency stock release could pull it back below $95.
outlook.watch: Saudi statements on Ras Tanura, Middle East headlines, and weekly U.S. inventory data.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Down 1.1% today to about $613; down about 12% since its Oct. 21 earnings
stocks.why: Meta's Q3 revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, but the stock fell 7% the next day as it said it would keep investing aggressively in AI in 2027. Investors also worried about rising debt (long-term debt hit $80.9 billion), a board committee warning about credit ratings, a new non-voting share class, and a $9.9 billion legal settlement charge that cut its operating margin to 20%.
stocks.meaning: The stock is now about 21% below its 52-week high as the market questions how much AI spending will pay off. It will likely move in sympathy with tonight's Microsoft and Alphabet capex commentary.

outlook.bullCase: Evidence from peers that AI spending is driving revenue, or Meta clarifying its funding plans, could spark a rebound toward $650–$700.
outlook.bearCase: Further worries about debt or capex could send it toward its 52-week low near $520.
outlook.watch: MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN capex commentary, any credit-rating actions, and details on the Class C shares.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.move: Down 0.6% today to about $528; down 0.9% this week, ahead of earnings tonight
stocks.why: Microsoft reports after today's close, with investors focused on Azure cloud growth and how much it plans to spend on AI data centres. It recently offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees, a sign it is trying to offset those costs.
stocks.meaning: Earnings days often bring 5–10% moves for mega-caps. Microsoft is about 4% below its 52-week high going in.

outlook.bullCase: Faster Azure growth and steady margins could push it to a new high above $551.
outlook.bearCase: A capex jump without faster cloud growth could send it back toward $500.
outlook.watch: Azure growth rate, capex guidance and margin outlook tonight.

stocks.name: Alphabet

stocks.meaning: Alphabet is about 21% below its 52-week high, so expectations are lower than for some peers, which can cushion disappointments.

outlook.bullCase: Strong cloud and search numbers could lift it back toward $345–$355.
outlook.bearCase: Weak ad growth or a big capex increase could push it toward $300.
outlook.watch: Google Cloud revenue growth, search ad trends and capex guidance tonight.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.move: Up 1.1% today to about $346; up 2.5% this week
stocks.why: Broadcom is extending Tuesday's chip rally after reports that its CEO helped arrange a $63 billion bank-consortium financing structure for AI computing. SK Hynix's record results and its forecast of a memory shortage lasting into 2030 also lifted the whole chip group.
stocks.meaning: Chipmakers are benefiting from strong AI demand data, but they are also the first to fall if Big Tech signals spending cuts. Broadcom is still about 30% below its 52-week high.

outlook.bullCase: Confirmation of strong AI capex from Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon could extend the rebound toward $375.
outlook.bearCase: Any capex cuts or a hawkish Fed could send it back toward $320.
outlook.watch: Big Tech capex guidance and chip-sector news.

stocks.name: Coinbase
stocks.move: Down 1.5% today to about $159; down about 10% this week
stocks.why: Coinbase is sliding ahead of its Q3 results Thursday after the close, where analysts expect a loss of about $0.22 a share on revenue around $1.2 billion, down about 36% from a year ago. Low crypto volatility has cut trading volumes, and Robinhood's results showing crypto revenue down 55% added to concerns. A recent analytics-vendor breach exposed some customer contact details, though Coinbase said funds were not affected.
stocks.meaning: Coinbase is about 56% below its 52-week high and close to its low near $139. Results will show whether its subscription and stablecoin income can make up for weak trading.

outlook.bullCase: Better-than-feared trading revenue and growth in USDC and prediction-market income could spark a relief rally toward $175–$185.
outlook.bearCase: Another revenue miss could push it toward the $139 low.
outlook.watch: Q3 results Thursday, trading volume data, and bitcoin's direction.
